content: Pre-Requisite To use the new Forms UI, you must have the updated Events January 2025 Salesforce release. Forms UI The new Forms UI is fully integrated into the Events package, offering a seamless, user-friendly experience for creating and managing {{variable.Object_Form}} s. The updated interface simplifies workflows, enhances functionality, and delivers powerful new capabilities to Event Organizers. Use the new Forms UI for a variety of scenarios including: Conferences: Build detailed {{variable.Object_Form}} s with conditional logic that adapts to {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s’ preferences, such as {{variable.Object_Session}} selection or dietary requirements. Workshops: Create multi-page {{variable.Object_Form}} s with nested questions that reveal specific options based on user input. Community Events: Simplify group registrations with dynamic {{variable.Object_Form}} s that cater to different {{variable.Object_Attendee}} types. Sessions: Customize the registration experience by asking questions of only those {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s who sign up for a specific {{variable.Object_Session}} in the context of the Session-selection step. Improved Functionality Nested Conditional Questions Build dynamic {{variable.Object_Form}} s with conditions nested multiple levels deep. Automatically reveal or hide questions based on {{variable.Object_Attendee}} input, enabling highly customized workflows. Drag-and-Drop Reordering Reorder questions and nested conditions visually using drag-and-drop functionality. Ensure a logical flow to your {{variable.Object_Form}} s, reducing {{variable.Object_Attendee}} confusion. Enhanced Preview Interface View {{variable.Object_Form}} s exactly as they will appear to {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s. Navigate and verify nested conditions effortlessly. Clone Forms Duplicate entire {{variable.Object_Form}} s or configurations to save time and maintain consistency across Events. Expand/Collapse Navigation Expand or collapse sections of complex {{variable.Object_Form}} s for easier navigation, editing, and management. User-Friendly Design Drag-and-drop tools, streamlined previews, and clear navigation make form creation intuitive for users of all skill levels. About Forms Forms can be used during three different stages of an {{variable.Object_Event}} : pre-registration, post-registration, and post-event (survey). You can decide the format of a question and if it is optional or dependent on the answer to a different question. The answers to these questions can help you create a unique experience and give you an insight into the voices and opinions of your {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s. Pre-Registration The pre-registration {{variable.Object_Form}} or questions appear during the registration process. Pre-registration {{variable.Object_FormElement}} s can be added at the {{variable.Object_Event}} level or to individual {{variable.Object_EventItem}} s but not both. If they are added to both, there will be duplicate questions on the registration form. Pre-registration {{variable.Object_FormElement}} s set at the {{variable.Object_EventItem}} level can also be used with {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_VisibilityCo}} to ask specific questions to specific {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s. The Forms for Sessions feature can only be used during the pre-registration phase of the Event checkout process. Post-Registration Post-registration questions are sent to invited or registered {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s via their {{variable.AttendeeLink}} . Post-registration {{variable.Object_Form}} s are presented to {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s after they register for an {{variable.Object_Event}} . {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s can access these questions by clicking their {{variable.AttendeeLink}} . Surveys Post-event questions are sent after the {{variable.Object_Event}} is over and give {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s an opportunity to provide feedback about the {{variable.Object_Event}} . Surveys can be added to the {{variable.Object_Event}} , {{variable.Object_EventItem}} , or {{variable.Object_Attendee}} records. Surveys can be sent automatically by using the process builder or a flow. About Form Elements A {{variable.Object_FormElement}} contains the question(s) in a {{variable.Object_Form}} . There are 14 types of {{variable.Object_FormElement}} s. Big List Group - use for very large picklists with thousands of options like postal codes. Checkbox - ask a question that can be answered with a check. Date - ask your {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s to enter a specific date. Divider - add a blank space between questions or include more information Email - ask your {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s to enter an email address. File Upload - ask your {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s to upload a specific type of file. Hidden - use to map a hidden {{variable.Object_FormElement}} to a field on a different object. Multi-Select Picklist - allow your {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s to select multiple answers Number - ask your {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s to enter a certain type of number. UTM Parameter - add tags to a URL to create Google Analytics data. Picklist - ask your {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s to select one answer from a list of options. Text - ask your {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s a question that requires a written answer. Text (30,000) - ask your {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s a question that requires a very long response. URL - ask your {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s to enter a URL that answers your question. Click here for information about setting up the {{variable.Object_FormElement}} types. Form Element Fields The following fields are on the {{variable.Object_FormElement}} object. {{variable.Field_FormElement_Type}} - defines the type of question you want to ask. {{variable.Field_FormElement_Required}} - defines whether the question is required. {{variable.Field_FormElement_QuestiontoAs}} - defines the questions you want to ask your {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s. {{variable.Field_FormElement_SuppQuesInfo}} - this information helps clarify the question in the {{variable.Field_FormElement_QuestiontoAs}} field. It appears below the primary question and can include any rich text, such as hyperlinks, colors, and formatting. {{variable.Field_FormElement_MapstoObject}} - defines where the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} 's answer will go. If you select "Contact" from this picklist, the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} 's answer will be defined on the {{variable.Object_Contact}} object. {{variable.Field_FormElement_MapstoField}} - defines the field on the object where the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} 's answer will go. If you set {{variable.Field_FormElement_MapstoObject}} to {{variable.Object_Contact}} and select "City" from the picklist, the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} 's answer will be stored in the {{variable.Object_Contact}} ’s City field. {{variable.Field_FormElement_DefaultValue}} - defines the default value for a picklist, text field, etc. when an {{variable.Object_Attendee}} opens the registration form. {{variable.Field_FormElem_DefaCheckboxVal}} - defines the default value (checked or unchecked) for a checkbox question. {{variable.Field_FormElement_Hint}} - defines the help text for the question. {{variable.Field_FormElem_WhenQuestionSho}} - defines whether to add conditional questions. Conditional Questions Limitation: A single {{variable.Object_FormElement}} can only include up to 200 Conditional {{variable.Object_FormElement}} s (questions). A conditional question is a {{variable.Object_FormElement}} . The answer to a conditional question determines which question ( {{variable.Object_FormElement}} ) will be asked next. This type of question can include multiple levels of nested conditional questions, giving Event Organizers the ability to gather complex information. The following types of {{variable.Object_FormElement}} s allow for conditional questions, including multiple levels of nested conditional questions. Checkbox Date Email Multi-Select Picklist Picklist Text Text (30,000) URL Click here to create a {{variable.Object_Form}} with {{variable.Object_FormElement}} s.
